title: The Last Protocol Again
premise: Astrid Villalobos, caretaker of the abandoned Svalbard-Orbital Seed Vault, survives the system-wide nine-second gravity flicker and discovers it was a weapon test disguised as an accident — a test that erased an entire mining station's crew and rewrote every record to hide the massacre. When the flicker's designers begin hunting anyone whose memories survived the record-wipe, Astrid must choose between the loyalty they owe to the smuggler crew who raised them and the truth owed to four hundred dead miners. The novel ends with Astrid broadcasting the true records from the vault's ancient transmitters, sacrificing their own archived memories to do it, and surviving — changed, half-remembered, and finally honest.
about_author: Mirabel Lockridge is the pen name of a former logistics dispatcher who spent a decade coordinating freight through politically contested shipping lanes, an experience that shapes the novel's claustrophobic orbital geography. They write near-future science fiction about ordinary workers caught inside extraordinary cover-ups.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. During a routine cargo run from the seed vault, gravity across the entire system stutters for nine seconds. Astrid's ship, the Marrow, drifts through wreckage that official charts say shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: unease hardening into dread as Astrid realizes the flicker wasn't natural.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Back at the vault, Astrid catalogs the wreckage: hull plating matching the mining station Kestrel's Promise, which records insist was decommissioned safely years ago with all hands evacuated. Emotional beat: the loneliness of caretaking curdling into the vertigo of being the only witness.

chapters.title: Crew of the Marrow
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV through Astrid's eyes. Astrid presents the evidence to the smuggler crew who raised them: gruff captain Odile, engineer Tam, and pilot Sef. Odile orders them to drop it — survival first. Emotional beat: Astrid's first taste of loyalty pulling against truth.

chapters.title: Records That Lie Politely
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid cross-references archive feeds and finds the Kestrel's Promise records are internally consistent, beautifully so — too consistent. A memory fragment of their own, of a distress ping twelve years ago, contradicts them. Emotional beat: self-doubt as the first casualty of a cover-up.

chapters.title: The Man Who Remembered Wrong
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef admits he crewed a rescue ship near Kestrel's Promise years back and remembers bodies, not evacuation. But his own logs now show the evacuation. Someone is editing minds as well as databases. Emotional beat: horror at discovering memory itself is contested territory.

chapters.title: Buyers and Buryers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A broker offers Odile a fortune for any 'anomalies' from the flicker — and a quiet threat for keeping them. Odile recognizes the buyer's corporate watermark as the same one funding the vault's decommissioning. Emotional beat: Odile's protective instinct weaponized against her crew's curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Remember
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Deep in the vault's legacy systems, Astrid finds the seed bank's environmental logs: nine seconds of gravitational anomaly recorded twelve years ago too — the first test, smaller, on Kestrel's Promise itself. Emotional beat: revelation that this has happened before, and the vault has been keeping the receipts all along.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with flashback. Astrid recalls being hired young, unqualified, by a vault administrator who vanished soon after. The administrator's final message, encrypted in a seed manifest, surfaces: 'If gravity ever blinks, you're the backup.' Emotional beat: Astrid realizing their whole caretaking life was someone's contingency plan.

chapters.title: The Wipe Team
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam intercepts a boarding party posing as inspectors — the same watermark, armed, scanning for 'residual mnemonic contamination.' Tam hides the evidence core inside a seed canister. Emotional beat: fear becoming resolve; the crew stops being bystanders.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Priced
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The broker raises the offer: enough to retire the whole crew forever, in exchange for the canister and Astrid's silence. Odile, drowning in debt the crew doesn't know about, nearly takes it. Emotional beat: the antagonist isn't the corporation — it's exhaustion.

chapters.title: Half a Confession
chapters.summary: Astrid and Odile's POV, alternating. Odile confesses her debts; Astrid confesses they've already copied the evidence and sent a fragment to a journalist relay. The fight is quiet and devastating. Emotional beat: loyalty strained to transparency — the crew either fractures or becomes family for real.

chapters.title: The Second Blink
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Gravity flickers again — longer, targeted, centered on the vault. The wipe team isn't testing anymore; they're erasing. Astrid's own memories of the last three days begin to blur. Emotional beat: the clock starts — Astrid is being edited in real time.

chapters.title: Analog Salvation
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam discovers the vault's ancient seed-storage cold systems are shielded from the mnemonic weapon: analog, offline, dumb. They can store the truth physically where the wipe can't reach — if they can move it before the next pulse. Emotional beat: hope found in obsolete things.

chapters.title: Sef's Run
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef flies the Marrow through contested orbits to physically retrieve the journalist's confirmation of the leaked fragment — and finds the journalist's relay dark, the journalist 'evacuated.' Emotional beat: grief and the understanding that everyone who helps them disappears politely.

chapters.title: Four Hundred Names
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Inside the shielded core, Astrid recovers the Kestrel's Promise crew manifest — four hundred miners, including children born in the tunnels. Among them: the vanished vault administrator's sister. Emotional beat: abstraction becomes personal; the dead acquire faces.

chapters.title: The Offer They Can't Refuse
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The corporation stops pretending: full amnesty, debts erased, new identities — if the crew hands over Astrid and the core. Odile stalls, buys time, and secretly begins planning something she doesn't tell Astrid. Emotional beat: love expressed as conspiracy.

chapters.title: What Odile Did
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid discovers Odile has sold a decoy of the core to buy the Marrow a clear escape window — and volunteered to stay behind as the distraction. Emotional beat: the loyalty-versus-truth theme made flesh; Astrid refuses to let Odile pay alone.

chapters.title: Broadcast from the Cold
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Climax begins. Astrid initiates the vault's legacy transmitters, but broadcasting requires unlocking the mnemonic archive — exposing Astrid's own memories to the same weapon. Tam rigs a partial shield; it will cost Astrid twelve years of stored memory. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Ninth Second
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The wipe team hits the vault with a full pulse as Astrid broadcasts. Odile's diversion buys ninety seconds. Sef and Tam hold the Marrow in the blast shadow of the vault to shield the transmission. Emotional beat: every character's loyalty cashed out in action at once.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Incomplete
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The broadcast lands: relay stations, mining colonies, and one honest auditor receive the true records. The corporation's story collapses publicly. Astrid wakes with gaps — faces they love feel like strangers. Emotional beat: victory that feels like amputation.

chapters.title: Relearning the Crew
chapters.summary: Sef and Tam's POV. The crew stays. They reintroduce themselves to Astrid daily — names, jokes, debts forgiven, Odile alive and limping. Astrid keeps written records now, analog, in their own hand. Emotional beat: tenderness rebuilt deliberately, memory as a gift others give you.

chapters.title: The Keeper's New Protocol
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Months later, the vault is repurposed as an independent archive for records corporations can't touch. Astrid, still missing pieces, writes the final entry: some things must be kept where forgetting can't reach them. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — truth survived, at a price worth paying.
